Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:5: In Sefer Chasidim (siman 14) it is written, on the root of love, that in order to serve with joy a person should take a lesson from flesh and blood: if he knew of something that was the king's will, he would not rest nor be still until he fulfilled the king's will — though he is but a worm and a maggot like the king himself — and he would rejoice with great joy that his deeds came before the king; how much more so, for the will of the Creator, who lives and endures, should he labor and seek how to accomplish and fulfill His commanded will. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:6: Further he should think and say in his heart: behold, the entire host of heaven perform their service with joy, glad and rejoicing to do the will of their Maker, and their supernal service is doubly greater than our own service — for the celestial spheres never cease from their motion, and likewise the sun forever circles, and every morning when it goes forth, it goes forth with joy, as it is said (Psalms 19:6), "it rejoices like a mighty man," and it sings before the Omnipresent — as our sages, of blessed memory, explained that they say the psalm "Give thanks to the Lord, call upon His name" (Psalms 105). And so it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Vayakhel 196a), in these words: and when the sun takes up [its journey] in its spheres, it opens with a pleasant voice and sings a song — what does it say? "Give thanks to the Lord, call upon His name," etc., "sing to Him a new song," etc. And Israel praise the Holy One, blessed be He, by day along with the sun, this being what is written (Psalms 72:5), "they shall fear You along with the sun" — and although this verse has already been explained [elsewhere], Rabbi Elazar said: were it not that people's hearts are sealed and their eyes closed, they could not withstand all the sweetness of the sun's sphere as it takes up its journey. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:7: Further they said in Midrash Tanchuma (Acharei 9): this is what Scripture says (Psalms 113:3), "from the rising of the sun to its setting, the Name of the Lord is praised" — from the hour the sun rises until it sets, it praises the Holy One, blessed be He. And so you find, at the time Joshua stood in Giv'on and wished to silence it, he did not say "sun in Giv'on, stand still," but rather "sun in Giv'on, be silent [dom]" — because every moment it travels, it praises the Holy One, blessed be He, and every moment it praises, it has strength to stand [travel]; therefore Joshua said to it, "be silent." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:8: One who heard and saw testified to me about people who went to the land of India to see the place where the sun rises and shines forth. Two went, and one returned mute — the one who drew close enough to hear the melody of the sun's sound died, and the other became mute, and this one, upon his return, related this in writing. And our sages, of blessed memory, likewise said in Sanhedrin regarding Sennacherib, that he made them hear the sound of the sun's sphere.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:9: In the manner that the sun sings, the supernal beings too sing and praise the Cause of all causes, whether among the emanated, the created, the formed, or the made — for all that the Holy One, blessed be He, created, He created only for His glory, as it is said (Isaiah 43:7), "all who are called by My name, for My glory I created him, I formed him, I even made him" — and "glory" is praise and song, as in (Psalms 29:9), "and in His Temple, all say, glory." And our sages, of blessed memory, so explained in Midrash Tehillim (mizmor 19), in these words: "the heavens declare" — this is what Scripture says (Proverbs 16:4), "the Lord has made everything for His own purpose" — for His praise, as it says (Psalms 147:7), "sing to the Lord with thanksgiving" — another interpretation, for His testimony, etc. — and he says further there: another interpretation, all the Lord's works are for His praise — for everything praises Him for His works and His deeds, and all His works praise Him. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:10: To this David the king, peace be upon him, referred in the psalm (ibid. 148:1), "praise the Lord from the heavens," etc., "praise Him, all His angels, praise Him, all His hosts, praise Him, sun and moon" — and it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Pekudei 232a), in these words: "Hallelujah, praise the Lord from the heavens" — this is the beginning of the six directions to spread downward, for this is the secret standing to be asked, as it is said, "for ask now of the former days that were before you," etc. (Deuteronomy 4:32) — up to here there is permission to ask; from here on it does not stand to be asked, for it is a hidden and concealed place. Therefore, "praise the Lord from the heavens, praise Him in the heights" — these are the two sides that are the height of the beginning, right and left, and from here all the others spread downward in the secret of the grades, to be properly arranged. "Praise Him, all His angels" — these are the two supports [legs] that stand beneath the body to bear the body upon them; come and see, those supports the body rests upon stand here in the secret of angels, for they need to be sent from place to place, and from this secret emerge those called angels, who are sent to travel in their Master's mission from place to place. "Praise Him, all His hosts" — this is the place from which emerge all the supernal holy armies, the secret of the letter of the holy covenant, which is imprinted on all the other myriads, as we said, as it is written, "the Lord of hosts is His name" — a sign among all the other armies and myriads. "Praise Him, sun and moon" — in this stands this secret, and it is the sun that gives light, and in it stand the supernal stars that shine, and constellations, as we have established. Afterward it returns above, to that place standing at the height of heights, and there is the sounding of the whole. Afterward, "praise the Lord from the earth," corresponding to these, "fire and hail." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:11: His intent is that "praise the Lord from the heavens" refers to the six extremities in general; "praise Him in the heights" is Chesed and Gevurah; "praise Him, all His angels" is Netzach and Hod — and as for why he called them angels, he said the reason is that angels are those sent from place to place, and their source is from the supernal thighs; "praise Him, all His hosts" corresponds to Yesod; "praise Him, sun and moon" corresponds to Tiferet and Malchut; "praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the waters above the heavens" — these are the first three [sefirot]. Afterward it descends below, to the physical elements: "praise the Lord from the earth," "sea monsters and all depths, fire and hail."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:12: There is no difficulty as to why the praise of the created and formed beings [briah/yetzirah] is not mentioned — for they are already mentioned in the praise "praise Him, all His angels, praise Him, all His hosts." And it would seem more fitting to mention "His hosts" first and then "His angels" — but the order was necessitated by the order of the attributes. Thus all existing things are included.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:13: How much more so those below them, all of which give song and praise to the Cause of causes — for even Keter, at the height of heights, the sounding of the whole, of it is said, "praise Him, heavens of heavens," and the verse afterward says, "let them praise the Name of the Lord, for He commanded and they were created" — and this Name YHVH, we must say, is the first Name attached to the Cause of causes, which is great and rules, etc., as explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1. The praise and glory is for having brought them into existence and created them from nothing into being; this is "for He commanded and they were created" — and this matter applies even to Keter, for it too is emanated, though not with the term "command" — and therefore you find the shofar-note reversed in the word "ki" [for], and a pause-note [tirchah] on the word "hu" [He]; understand this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:14: It is found in the books of the opponents [i.e., certain esoteric works] that there is a certain prince above, upon the Throne, who has a thousand mouths, and in each mouth a thousand tongues, and with each and every tongue he gives song and praise to his Maker, and he is called Yo'achatzatzbiron — and this prince is explained in the Tikkunim (beginning of p. 135) regarding his greatness; see there. And in Sefer Brit Menuchah several supernal princes are explained whose names end in "Hon" and "Ron" — the reason being that they are appointed over song, singing, and praise, and these are called "Alamot Shir" (Psalms 46:1) — maidens appointed over song.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:15: On this, the Men of the Great Assembly instituted for us (the Nishmat prayer), "were our mouths as full of song as the sea, and our tongues of joyous song as its many waves," etc. — the meaning being that the supernal sea sings a song, as it says (Psalms 30:13), "so that glory may sing praise to You and not be silent," and in the manner of (ibid. 83:2), "O God, do not be silent" — for she always arouses song to unify Abba and Imma, as my master explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance (ch. 20), and her waves are the winds of the Throne within her, which likewise arouse song.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:16: With this one may understand what is explained in the Zohar (parashat Noach 69b) on the verse (Psalms 89:10), "when its waves rise, You still them" [alt. "praise them"] — in these words: "You praise them" literally — praise is theirs, because they rise in longing to see; from here, whoever longs to gaze and to know, even though he cannot, praise is his, and all praise him. — end of quotation. The meaning is that the supernal winds within the Throne go and run and lift themselves up in order to see and attain, through the supernal light, that which is above their attainment; and although they turn back, unable to attain what is above their rank, nevertheless it is praise for them that they have the desire to attain more and to cling to the supernal light.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:17: So too souls, after their passing, give thanks and praise to the Holy One, blessed be He, as explained in the Zohar (parashat Terumah 142a), in these words: this soul, at the time the spirit descends from the supernal light to dwell in the Garden of Eden, shines and sparkles — it [the spirit], when it stands in the grave, is fashioned in the image it had within the body originally, and all those bones in that same image of theirs give praise and thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He, this being what is written (Psalms 35:10), "all my bones shall say, Lord, who is like You" — it does not say "say" [present] but "shall say" [future/continuous]; and were permission given to the eye to see, on the night the Sabbath departs, and on the nights of the New Moon and the festivals, they would see them in their images upon the graves, giving thanks and praising the Holy One, blessed be He — but the foolishness of human beings prevents [this vision], etc. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:18: Since all the supernal beings arouse song out of their longing to cling to Him, in like manner man too must arouse song and praise to gladden his Maker, and in order to cling to his Maker — for song brings about clinging. And this is when he remembers His abundant favors and kindnesses toward him, as we say, "were our mouths as full of song as the sea, we would not suffice to thank You for even one of the thousand thousands of thousands of miracles and wonders You performed for us and for our fathers, and the spirit and soul You breathed into our nostrils, and the tongue You placed in our mouths — they shall thank and bless and sing to Your Name, our King."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:19: David the king, peace be upon him, intended this in saying (Psalms 31:8), "I will be glad and rejoice in Your kindness, for You have seen my affliction" — here the joy comes from the side of Chesed, that He did good for him. On account of this David was always singing, and he would command us to arouse song and joy, saying (ibid. 33:1), "sing joyfully, O righteous, in the Lord," "sing to Him a new song" (ibid. 33:3).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:20: Likewise, you find that whenever a miracle was performed for Israel they would immediately sing a song — "then Israel sang" (Exodus 15:1), "and Devorah sang" (Judges 5:1) — and it is impossible for a miracle to occur without the attribute of Chesed participating in it; and so it is explained in parashat Vayikra (8a) on the verse (Psalms 100:2), "serve the Lord with gladness" — that from the priest's own side the joy comes, in these words: joy is established in the priest, because he is always far from judgment, and the priest must always be found with a shining countenance, always rejoicing, more than the whole people. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:21: In the Zohar (parashat Vayikra 8b), they asked regarding the verse "serve the Lord with gladness," etc.: one who has sinned and transgressed a negative commandment of the Torah, his rectification is to bring a sacrifice, confess, and grieve — and if he weeps, all the better for him — if so, where is his joy and song? They answered: while the Temple stood, this matter depended on the priest and the Levite — for the priest, the man of Chesed, is the one full of joy, and the Levite sings — thus joy and song are found. And afterward they asked, of blessed memory: now that there is no sacrifice, one who sins before his Master and returns to Him surely does so with bitterness of soul, with grief, with weeping, with a broken spirit — how then can joy and song be established, since they are not found in him? Rather, they have already established that the praises of one's Master and the joy of Torah and the song of Torah — this is joy and song.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:22: He further explained there another interpretation, that joy and song are Yesod and Malchut, and the intent is that one's intention be to unify these attributes, of which our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 8a), a person should always enter [the synagogue] the space of two doorways [before praying] — and they elaborated further in the Zohar (parashat Terumah 165a) on the resolution of this question; see there. Thus the general principle of joy, according to this, is that the Name has granted him to be among His servants who unify Him — which not every person merits.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:23: According to the plain sense, the joy a person should arouse in his prayer, especially if he is in the synagogue or study hall, is in the reality of prayer — for prayer is a supernal necessity, and the proof is that from it a crown is made for the King of the universe; and it is fitting that a person say in his heart, from where have I merited to give a crown to the King of the universe, except that the King, in His abundant kindness, has drawn me near to Him — therefore it is fitting that I perform His service with joy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:24: Also regarding the reality of prayer, the Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Zohar, parashat Terumah 131b) that three camps of angels stand in the synagogue for the rectification of prayer: one camp are those angels who sing with Israel by day, and these rectify all the hymns, because there is another company that sings by night, and these do not stand with Israel by day. The second camp are those who stand at every Kedushah that Israel sanctify below, and it says: and in their dominion are all those who are aroused in all those firmaments through that prayer of Israel. The third camp are the seven maidens fit to be given to her — these being the seven supernal halls that are arranged in the Yotzer prayer. And it says: and all of them are arranged according to the order of Israel, arranged below, which are the songs and praises, and through that prayer that Israel pray. — end of quotation. Here it is stated that the whole rectification of the supernal camps and the rectification of the Shechinah with her camps depend on the prayer of Israel. And so it says further there (p. 132): for there is no Kedushah above except if there is Kedushah below, as it is said (Leviticus 22:32), "and I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel" — and the rest of his words we quoted in the Gate of Holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:25: Standing in the synagogue, one should be joyful to stand in the House of the Lord, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 122:1), "I rejoiced when they said to me, let us go to the House of the Lord," and he says (ibid. 84:3), "my soul longs, indeed it faints, for the courts of the Lord; my heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:26: In engaging with Torah he should be joyful, as it is said (Berachot ch. 4, mishnah 2), Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah used to pray upon entering the study hall and upon leaving it, and he said: upon leaving, I give thanks for my portion; and it is explained in the Gemara (Berachot 28b) that he would say, "we thank You, O Lord our God, for placing our portion among those who sit in the study hall," etc., "I run to the life of the World to Come" — in its place we shall elaborate on its explanation, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:27: Further, our sages, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 117a) regarding Elisha, who said (II Kings 3:15), "and now bring me a minstrel," etc., "and the hand of the Lord came upon him" — this teaches that the Shechinah does not rest through laziness, nor through sadness, nor through laughter, nor through levity, nor through idle conversation and idle words, but through the joy of a commandment, as it is said, "and now bring me a minstrel," etc. Rabbi Yehudah said in the name of Rav: likewise for a matter of halachah [study]. Rav said: likewise for a good dream. Is that so? [etc., until] he would sit in awe and then begin the discourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:28: In engaging with the commandments he should be joyful, for the commandments are the king's ornaments, and He is adorned with them; it is fitting that one be joyful, especially when he knows what rectification he performs by doing that commandment and what benefit it does for his soul — then he will be even more joyful, and we shall elaborate further in the Gate of Commandments. Of this it is said (Psalms 19:9), "the precepts of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:29: Especially regarding charity, one must be joyful in giving it, for through it he clings to the Shechinah, as it is said (ibid. 17:15), "I, in righteousness [tzedek], shall behold Your face," as we shall elaborate in its place. Do you not see that David the king, peace be upon him, and Israel, when they donated for the building of the Temple, did so with joy, as it is said (I Chronicles 29:9), "and the people rejoiced over their donations, for they donated with a whole heart to the Lord," and David the king too rejoiced with great joy? It follows that a commandment performed with a good heart itself gives joy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:30: In receiving every person with a pleasant countenance there is a secret, as explained in the Idra (Idra, parashat Naso 133a), in these words: we have learned, what is meant by (Isaiah 61:10), "I will greatly rejoice in the Lord" — of the Ancient of Days it is said, for this is the joy of the whole. — end of quotation. And further there it says that from the two supernal faces of the Ancient Ones the face of Ze'ir Anpin is illuminated below, and of the supernal faces it is said (Proverbs 16:15), "in the light of the King's face is life." And it says afterward: we have learned, when these two apples [cheeks] are revealed, Ze'ir Anpin is seen in joy, and all the lamps below shine, and all the worlds rejoice and are complete in all completeness, and all rejoice and shine, and all goodness never ceases — end of quotation, as pertains here. Here it is explained that all realities need joy, that they are aroused in all the worlds from the supernal faces; and thus a person's receiving every other person with a pleasant, shining countenance indicates the face of Ze'ir Anpin illuminated by the supernal faces, which is the supernal completeness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:31: How much more so if he receives the face of a sage or his own teacher, whose reception is like the reception of the Shechinah's own face (Yerushalmi, Eruvin ch. 5, halachah 1) — that it must be with joy. Our sages, of blessed memory, said in Tanchuma (Shemot 27), regarding Aaron, of whom it is said (Exodus 4:14), "and he shall see you and rejoice in his heart" — and it does not say simply "and rejoice," but "and rejoice in his heart"; Rashbi said: the heart that rejoiced in his brother's greatness shall wear the Urim and Tummim, as it is said, "and you shall put the breastplate of judgment," etc., "and they shall be upon Aaron's heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:32: Joy of the festivals — it is already known what our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Pesachim 109a), that on the festival a person is obligated to rejoice with meat and wine, he and his household, etc. And the reason the festival is called "ushpiza" [a guest] is that it comes from time to time, and just as a guest must be received with a pleasant countenance, so must the festivals be received; and the reason is that on the festivals a new light is revealed, as the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in parashat Emor regarding the "holy convocations."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:33: In the Tikkunim (58b) it says, in these words: further, the Shechinah is called "chag" [festival] at all the appointed times and festivals — the festival of the three pilgrimage feasts, of which it is said (Exodus 23:14), "three times [regalim] you shall celebrate a feast [tachog] for Me in the year" — and for her sake, "all your males shall appear" — to fulfill "remember" and "observe" — "remember" for the male, "observe" for the female. All those who go to gaze upon the Shechinah must give her a gift, this being what is written (Deuteronomy 16:16), "and none shall appear before the Lord empty-handed" — and one must rejoice in her, this being what is written (ibid. 16:14), "and you shall rejoice in your feast," for she is called the joy of the Holy One, blessed be He; and whoever goes to see her must guard himself from sadness, which is Lilith, darkness, the sadness of the spleen [alt. Sheol], which is a blemish, and of it is said (Leviticus 21:18), "any man who has a blemish shall not approach." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:34: Especially on the festival of Sukkot, which is called "the time of our joy," as we say in our prayers, one must be joyful, especially while in the sukkah, as it is said in the Zohar (parashat Emor, end of p. 103), in these words: a person must rejoice on each and every day with a shining countenance, together with those guests who dwell with him. My master, may his rest be in Eden, was precise in noting that it says "each and every day," and does not say generally "during these seven days" — to show that on each and every day one must have a joy particular to itself, for the seven days are themselves the seven guests, so on each day there is its own particular guest, and one must show him joy. And it further says there: this is like Rav Hamnuna, who, when he entered the sukkah, would rejoice — the rest of his words need not be quoted, except that in the end he must rejoice the poor, for the portion of those guests destined to be invited belongs to the poor. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:35: Among the conditions of festival joy is that it not be joy through frivolity and outings, in the manner of the joy of the gentiles' festivals, as it is said (Hosea 9:1), "do not rejoice, O Israel, to exultation, like the peoples," but rather it should be in the joy of the festival itself, which is the days of the holy convocations, as explained above — like a person standing in darkness who rejoices when a new light comes to him; so too one must rejoice in the joy of Torah on the festival more than at other times, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yerushalmi, Shabbat ch. 15, halachah 3), that festivals were given to Israel only to engage in Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:36: Know that the reality of joy brings about union, for it is impossible for the effects to draw near to the cause unless there is joy between them, that the cause desires its effect to draw near to it, and likewise the effect's joy to be included in its cause, so as to be illuminated by it — this is "an offering [korban] to the Lord," explained in the Tikkunim (34b), which say, in these words: and when they draw near [in the offering], father joins with mother, son with daughter, each with his mate — the supernal Heh toward the Yod, the lower Heh toward the Vav — this is the ascending and descending offering; at that time (Ezekiel 37:7), "and the bones drew near, bone to its bone." And at the end of his words: and when it [the fire] descends toward the son, it is said of it (Leviticus 6:5), "and the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it" — it is kindled with the flames of love. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:37: The flames of love are precisely joy, and this is a fire coming from the left side, which is the wine that gladdens, and it is that which brings about the union; and so it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Korach 178b) regarding "and he shall serve the Levite, he [hu]" (Numbers 18:23), in these words: "he" [hu] completes the completion, that all become one. "He" — simply, to receive the Assembly of Israel, as it says (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head," in order to join the union together — who arouses the love? Say, HU ["He"]. — end of quotation. And there he explains several interpretations of the word HU; and by this interpretation, HU is in Binah, and from there the joy is aroused for the Assembly of Israel in union, so that the whole of Atzilut is unified in its complete wholeness as one. It follows that the essence of joy is the union and binding of the whole of Atzilut as one, and its illumination through the Emanator — for this is the whole of joy, that they all shine and unify as one, until the Emanator illumines them properly.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:38: With this introduction we may understand what the Psalmist, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 32:11), "rejoice in the Lord and exult, O righteous," and likewise (ibid. 35:9), "and my soul shall exult in the Lord" — for the essence of the soul's joy is in its being illuminated by the light of the whole of Atzilut, included within YHVH, as is known. And if we wish to interpret that the plain sense of the Name YHVH refers to Tiferet, this too is reconcilable, because then it draws supernal life from the One who gives life to all existing things, who is bound up with this Name, and all is one — for Tiferet includes all ten [sefirot] within the Name YHVH within it, and it is the light of all the colors; I have elaborated on this in its place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:39: Therefore, whoever wishes to gladden his soul should seclude himself part of the day to contemplate the greatness of the letters of YHVH, as we explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 5. Proof of this is what David the king, peace be upon him, said (ibid. 16:9), "I have set the Lord always before me; therefore my heart is glad, and my glory [kevodi] rejoices" — and "my glory" is the soul, and because the soul's emanation is from the Name YHVH, as it says (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the Lord your God," therefore, when contemplating the Name YHVH, the soul shines and is polished in wondrous brilliance, and it rejoices; and by the strength of that illumination it has the power to give some sparkle even to the flesh, so that "even my flesh shall dwell securely," that the worm shall not rule over it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:40: This is the rank of the righteous who cling to the Name of the Lord, that even in their death they are called living — for because of their attachment to the Name YHVH, which is the source of life, they impart some vitality even to the flesh, so that they are called living even in their death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:41: It may be explained that "my heart is glad" corresponds to the flesh, and "my glory" to the inwardness within it, and both of these were created through the Name YHVH, as explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 7. Therefore, after death, not only will the soul be bound to the root to which it was attached in its living life, so that even now it shall dwell securely, but even the flesh — since the flesh too was attached and rejoiced in YHVH, and the heart is the essence of all 248 limbs — it is fitting that the worm not rule over the whole flesh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:42: Now we may understand its saying (Psalms 33:1), "sing joyfully, O righteous, in the Lord" [ba-Hashem] — for it would seem more fitting to say "sing joyfully, O righteous, to the Lord" [la-Hashem], in the manner of (Psalms 105:2), "sing to Him, make music to Him," and it does not say "sing in Him." Rather, the matter may be explained in two ways: first, in the manner it says "righteous in YHVH," whose explanation is thus stated — that the righteous are now commanded that if they sing joyfully, their intent should be to unify the Name YHVH, and this is "ba-Hashem" — that this Name be before you, that you unify it, so that such song is complete clinging.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:43: It may also be said that the intent is that song in general brings about clinging. How so? For when a person recounts the praises of the King of the universe, in the manner of David the king's own praises, peace be upon him, and likewise the several praises of the Omnipresent that the pious Rabbi Yehudah HaLevi, peace be upon him, composed — the saying of them brings about the clinging of one's soul to his God, for the Holy One, blessed be He, desires that His greatness and glory be recounted, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 145:4), "one generation shall praise Your works to another," etc., "of the glorious splendor of Your majesty... I shall speak" — and most of the psalm speaks of this, that it is fitting to recount His praises, glory, greatness, and the like — and all these songs arouse desire and love between Israel and their Father in Heaven. The parable for this: a king of flesh and blood, when he hears that one of his servants recounts his praises and honor, surely the king will love him, for the king says, surely this one who recounts my praises surely loves me, and it is fitting that I too love him — and the parallel is understood. This is what is meant by "sing joyfully, O righteous" — when you sing joyfully, O righteous, you are immediately bound to YHVH. There is support for this from the division of the cantillation marks, that there is a pause-note [tirchah] on the word "tzaddikim" [righteous]. And as is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, p. 23b), that the song itself contains an allusion to YHVH, in these words: ten wheels [alt. strings] are the yod, corresponding to the ten fingers that strike in the melody five against five, and these are heh-heh that ascend into the yod, in the six grades that are the vav, in which they ascend and descend. — end of quotation. And further there: when the daughter [bat kol, or the letter beit] ascends in song, the eagle takes the yod in its mouth and upon its head, the vav in its body, the heh-heh in its wings — Adam: yod, heh; daleth-aleph, vav; aleph-vav, riding upon all. — end of quotation. With this, "ba-Hashem" may be understood — the intent being that the song itself is [structured] in YHVH, as alluded.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:44: It may further be explained regarding "ba-Hashem" through what we have explained several times, that the Name YHVH is patterned in man in every single limb, and even in his spirit — so the instruments of song in his mouth are [patterned after] YHVH, and through them he sings — and this is (Psalms 35:10), "all my bones shall say, Lord, who is like You."
